slides.title: 5 home energy myths you're probably still falling for

slides.myth: Crank the thermostat way up and the house warms up faster.
slides.fact: Your furnace heats at one speed no matter what number you pick. A higher setting just makes it overshoot and burn extra. Set the temperature you actually want.

slides.myth: A ceiling fan cools down the room.
slides.fact: Fans cool people, not rooms. The air stays the same temperature, the breeze just feels cooler on your skin. So turn it off when you leave.
slides.source: U.S. Department of Energy, via Popular Science

slides.myth: Closing the vents in rooms you don't use saves money.
slides.fact: It can actually waste energy. The system still pushes the same air, and the extra pressure forces more of it out through leaks in the ducts.
slides.source: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (2003), via Popular Science

slides.myth: Flipping LED lights on and off wears them out, so just leave them on.
slides.fact: Switching doesn't shorten an LED's life. That rule came from old fluorescent tubes. Leaving the room? Turn them off.
slides.source: U.S. Department of Energy, via Popular Science

slides.myth: Batteries last longer if you keep them in the fridge.
slides.fact: Battery makers say don't. Cold storage can cause condensation that damages them. Keep them at room temperature, about 68 to 78°F.
